$comment: ADAAAA-7765 - frame-derived ground truth for a rights-cleared basketball broadcast clip. Labels were read from the pixels only: the broadcast score overlays score digits were read at native frames, and the scoring instant is the first frame whose digits show the new score. No label comes from decide reason text, a detection model, or a soccer clip. Non-event windows lie strictly inside a score-stable interval and were liveness-checked at 320 px frames.

video.rights_holder: TBF (Turkish Basketball Federation) - uploader/author on Wikimedia Commons
video.attribution: TBF, Merkezefendi Belediyesi Denizli Basket - Samsunspor (24.01.2020), CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

segment.note: Q1 play; the committed clip-root copy is this segment cut with stream copy
segment.container: mp4 (h264 + aac), frame-accurate re-encode of source 1100-1950 s

video.frame_source: native 1280x720 frames decoded at 1 fps with ffmpeg; score-overlay crops read at native resolution
video.label_method: score-digit catalogue: 1 fps score-overlay crops, digit reads at every score state change, plus 320 px liveness frames for each non-event window
video.confidence_note: The scoring instant is bounded to +-1 s by the 1 fps frame grid (the first frame showing the new digits). A score delta of 1 is a free throw, 2 a field goal, 3 a three-pointer; the delta is the digit difference, not a shot-type label.
video.frames_dir: evals/basketball_val/frames/README.md (reproduction recipe; clip is a box-side clip-root artifact)

coverage.clip_span_note: 850 s (14 min 10 s) of continuous Q1 play, above the >= 5 min floor
coverage.floor: >= 5 min clip, >= 8 verified scoring events, >= 10 verified non-event windows
coverage.floor_met: yes for scoring events and non-event windows; one rights-cleared clip only
coverage.detection_slice: none - this manifest labels scoring events and windows, not detection-class boxes (see reference.detectionSlice in services/perceive/app/game_profile.py)
coverage.liveness_note: Each non-event window was liveness-checked on a 320 px frame; 7 are live play (the fair hard-negative set for the audio trigger FP rate) and 6 are dead-ball stoppages. The window's no-score claim is the score-digit constancy across the interval that contains it, not the liveness read.
